symptom: Moving the user-facing skills to `mdl 1` (decision 4 on ako/mxcli#714) exposed skill examples that never ran: `create snippet … (layout: …)`, `alter snippet … replace activity x with …`, a page sketched in pseudo-syntax (`layout X title 'Y' widgets (…)`) under a `-- check-skip` comment, attributes named `Id`/`CreatedDate`, a grant to a user role, `Repeat: Day`, java actions sharing one name, a catalog `SELECT … NOT IN (…)`. All were taught as copyable scripts; `make check-skill-mdl` and the conformance gate were green
cause: `scripts/check-skill-mdl.sh` checks only domain-model DDL and complete page/snippet statements, one statement at a time and as mdl 0; the conformance gate checks parse plus deprecations, with a per-file allowlist that absorbed these as `syntax`. Nothing ran `mxcli check` (which also validates semantics) on a whole example script, and a `-- check-skip` comment exempted a block forever
insight: Give a complete script the header and it becomes checkable as what it is: `mdl 1;` marks the block as a script, so a test can hold it to parse under mdl 1 with no allowlist, and a one-off extraction can run the real `mxcli check` on every header block (380 here, 18 failing semantically before this change). Blocks that are a deliberate WRONG example belong in ```text, not in the same fence as the RIGHT one. One trap in the checker itself: the page-widget wrapper parses almost anything (`list entities in M` is a widget), so a fragment must be judged in the FIRST context that parses it under either version, never accepted by whichever context happens to parse it under mdl 1
